official.deadline_note: Fall admission only. The November 1 priority scholarship deadline applies to all application plans: ED I, ED II and Regular Decision applicants who want scholarship consideration must have the completed BC application in by November 1 even though the ED II and RD deadlines are January 4. ED I applicants get decisions by December 15. The Admission site states finalists are notified in mid-January and interviewed on campus in mid-March; the GPSP FAQ still describes invitations with admission offers by February 1 and finalist visits in mid-February, so confirm the current finalist schedule with the programme once notified.
official.status_note: Boston College's current admission cycle is open (the Apply page posts 2026-27 supplemental questions and deadlines: ED I November 1, ED II January 4, RD January 4), and the programme states both Early Decision and Regular Decision candidates are considered for the scholarship as long as they meet the November 1 priority scholarship deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The programme 'annually awards full-tuition scholarships ... to 18 incoming freshman students,' and the Financial Aid page states 'the Presidential Scholarship is our only academic merit-based scholarship, covering full tuition for 18 qualified applicants each year.' Boston College publishes undergraduate tuition of $75,070 for the 2026-27 academic year (the International Applicants page lists $75,075 for the same year).

official.application_route: Submit the Common Application (ED I, ED II, or RD) to Boston College by November 1 and be automatically considered; no separate scholarship application or financial aid form is required.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to all applicants who apply by the November 1 deadline and meet the scholarship criteria, regardless of citizenship; Boston College cannot provide need-based financial aid to students who are not U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The programme FAQ confirms international students are eligible for this merit scholarship; international Scholars, however, cannot receive Boston College need-based aid and must be prepared to finance non-tuition costs in full (admitted international students verify finances via the Certification of Finances form before an I-20 is issued).
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction published. Candidates must apply to one of BC's four undergraduate academic divisions - Morrissey College of Arts and Sciences, Carroll School of Management, Lynch School of Education and Human Development, or Connell School of Nursing - and admitted Scholars enrol in one of the University's departmental honors programs.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal is required at application. Admitted Scholars enrol in a departmental honors program and must write an Honors Thesis.
official.duration: Four years at Boston College, provided Scholars maintain a 3.6 GPA and remain model citizens of the BC community.
official.description: The Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program is an undergraduate academic, merit program that annually awards full-tuition scholarships and fully-funded, GPSP-sponsored summer programs to 18 incoming freshman students. Boston College describes it as the University's only academic merit-based scholarship: 'a four-year, full-tuition scholarship awarded to 18 incoming first-year students.' Early Decision and Regular Decision applicants who submit their BC applications by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline are considered; there is no separate application, and only candidates for fall admission will be considered.
official.program_type: Four-year full-tuition undergraduate merit scholarship with an integrated honors education and funded summer experiences
official.english_requirement: Non-U.S. citizens must submit official TOEFL iBT, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores (test-optional policy does not cover English exams). Boston College lists recommended minimums of IELTS 7.5, Duolingo 130, and TOEFL iBT 100 (5.0 on the new six-point scale); exams are not superscored. The requirement is waived if English is the applicant's native language, the applicant attended a U.S. or majority-native-English school for at least three years in a traditional curriculum without ESOL coursework, or scores 650+ SAT EBRW / 29+ ACT English. InitialView interviews are encouraged for applicants from national schools in China.

applicant_utility.summary: This is Boston College's only academic merit scholarship, so admission itself doubles as the scholarship entry: submit the Common App, Writing Supplement and supplemental essay with everything complete by 1 November and you are automatically in the running for one of 18 full-tuition awards, chosen from roughly the top 1-2% of BC's applicant pool. Treat the 1 November date as immovable - ED II and Regular Decision applicants are considered for the scholarship only if the full application is already in by 1 November, and transfer or spring entry applicants are not eligible at all. Domestic Scholars who file for aid can have remaining demonstrated need met with grants, but the merit award itself pays tuition only, and international Scholars must personally fund housing, meals, fees and books because BC offers them no need-based aid. The package also carries a 3.6 GPA retention condition and a demanding three-summer programme of service learning, language immersion and a professional internship, so this is a commitment fit as much as a funding one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-1-2% academic performers with sustained leadership roles and a real community-service record who can get a November 1-ready Common Application out at the very start of senior year.
application_readiness_checklist: Fix your ED I / ED II / Regular Decision plan on the Common Application and submit everything by November 1 - scholarship consideration ends that day regardless of plan

Ask your counselor in September for the School Report and counselor recommendation, and line up two teacher evaluators from English, math, science, social studies or foreign language before the October rush
Confirm your official transcript will be sent by your school directly - BC will not accept academic credentials sent by students
Budget the $85 application fee, or request a Common Application fee waiver if it is a hardship
International applicants: register early for TOEFL iBT, IELTS or Duolingo so official scores arrive by November 1, remembering BC does not superscore English exams
Arts applicants: SlideRoom submissions must arrive by November 1 for ED I (January 4 for ED II/RD); applicants from national schools in China may add an InitialView interview by November 15 (ED I)
File your Mid-Year Grade Report as soon as grades are available if you are applying Regular Decision or are deferred from ED
common_rejection_risks: Missing the November 1 priority deadline - the single most common failure; the regular January deadlines carry no scholarship consideration
Assuming a separate GPSP application exists and waiting for it to open
Applying Regular Decision in January believing the April notification leaves time for scholarship review
Transfer or spring-entry candidates expecting consideration, which the programme excludes
Self-reported SAT/ACT scores that cannot be verified: enrolled students must submit official reports at matriculation and results are checked then
International applicants budgeting for tuition alone and discovering at admission that no need-based aid exists and a Certification of Finances must be funded before an I-20 is issued
Essays or supplemental responses that read as AI-generated - BC explicitly states content must be the applicant's own
Losing the award after enrollment by slipping below the required 3.6 GPA
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award pays tuition only (published 2026-27 rate $75,070). On BC's own 2025-26-2026-27 cost list, a Scholar still funds roughly $11,270 housing, $7,564 food, $1,354 mandatory fees and about $3,250 books and incidentals per year - around $20,000+ annually - unless they qualify for BC need-based aid (U.S. citizens and permanent residents only), in which case grant aid can close the remaining demonstrated need.
document_audit: Transcripts must arrive from the school itself - BC states it will not accept academic credentials submitted by students, so chase your counselor, not the mailroom
The Mid-Year Grade Report is a distinct required document for RD and deferred ED applicants and must be sent as soon as it is available, not at a later deadline
Teacher evaluations should come from two of the five core subject areas (English, social studies, science, math, foreign language) to be competitive
International files need official English-test reports sent directly by the testing agency; MyBest score compilations are not considered
The $85 fee or a waiver request must accompany the application or it will not be reviewed
alerts: ED is binding: if you apply Early Decision and are admitted you must withdraw all other applications, so use ED only if BC is genuinely your first choice - but remember scholarship consideration still requires the completed application by November 1 whichever plan you choose

Notification timing differs between BC pages (finalists mid-January with mid-March interviews on the Admission page vs by February 1 with mid-February visits on the GPSP FAQ) - plan travel and finances for either window once invited
First-year students pay one-time orientation ($670) and student ID ($50) charges beyond the standard cost of attendance
Retention requires a 3.6 GPA, so verify the load in your intended honours major is sustainable alongside the programme's summer commitments
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete Common Application (with BC Writing Supplement, supplemental response, counselor form, two teacher evaluations, transcript and fee) posted by November 1; consideration is automatic with no further materials; finalists are invited to Chestnut Hill at BC's expense for interviews and evaluative activities in the winter, with final decisions soon after the visit.
